qns_content.text: A mixture contains 1 mole of helium and 1 mole of oxygen at 300 K. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?

text_solutions:
For ideal gases, \(P = \frac{\mu RT}{V}\), partial pressure \(\propto \mu\) (since \(V\) and \(T\) are same).

Ratio \(\frac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{\mu_{\text{He}}}{\mu_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{1}{1} = 1\).

A steel rod of radius 0.005 m and length 1 m is compressed by a force producing a stress of 2 × 107 N/m2. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 1011 N/m2, what is the strain?

text_solutions:
Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain.

Strain: Strain = Stress / Y = (2 × 107) / (2 × 1011) = 1 × 10-4.

A wave on a string has an amplitude of 2 cm and a wavelength of 0.5 m. What is the maximum transverse speed of a particle on the string if its frequency is 20 Hz?

Amplitude \( a = 0.02 \, \text{m} \), frequency \( v = 20 \, \text{Hz} \).

Maximum speed: \( v_{\text{max}} = a \omega = 0.02 \times 40\pi \approx 2.51 \, \text{m/s} \).

qns_content.text: The density \( \rho \) of a substance depends on mass \( m \) and volume \( V \) as \( \rho = k m^a V^b \). Given \( [\rho] = [M L^{-3}] \), find \( a \) and \( b \).
A \( 40 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating downward at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
The scale shows the normal force.

Net force: \( N - mg = ma \), where \( a = -3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

\( N - 40 \times 10 = 40 \times (-3) \).

\( N - 400 = -120 \Rightarrow N = 280 \, \text{N} \).

qns_content.text: A force starts at \( 80 \, \text{N} \) over \( 6 \, \text{m} \), then decreases linearly to \( 20 \, \text{N} \) over \( 9 \, \text{m} \). What is the total work done?
A glass slab (\( n = 1.6 \)) of thickness \( 8 \, \text{cm} \) is placed over a coin. What is the apparent shift in the position of the coin?
In a single-slit diffraction experiment, if the slit width is \( 2.5 \, \mu\text{m} \) and the wavelength is \( 500 \, \text{nm} \), what is the angle of the first minimum?
A cyclist takes a circular turn of radius \( 5 \, \text{m} \) at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) on a level road with \( \mu_s = 0.4 \). Will the cyclist slip? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
Centripetal force required \( F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r} = \frac{m \times (15)^2}{5} = 45m \, \text{N} \).

Maximum friction \( f_{\text{max}} = \mu_s mg = 0.4 \times m \times 10 = 4m \, \text{N} \).

Compare: \( F_c = 45m \, \text{N} > f_{\text{max}} = 4m \, \text{N} \).

Since required force exceeds maximum friction, the cyclist will slip.

qns_content.text: A metal has a threshold frequency of \( 4.5 \times 10^{14} \, \text{Hz} \). What is the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted by light of frequency \( 6.0 \times 10^{14} \, \text{Hz} \)? (Take \( h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J s} \))
A solid sphere is subjected to a uniform hydraulic pressure of 2 × 107 N/m2. If the bulk modulus of the material is 1 × 1010 N/m2, what is the fractional change in volume?

text_solutions:
Bulk modulus: B = -p / (ΔV / V).

Rearrange: ΔV / V = -p / B.

Substitute: ΔV / V = -(2 × 107) / (1 × 1010) = -2 × 10-3.

Fractional change (magnitude): 2 × 10-3.

qns_content.text: The speed of an electron in the first orbit of a hydrogen atom is \( 2.2 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its speed in the second orbit?

A helicopter ascends at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) from \( 40 \, \text{m} \) height and releases a package after \( 5 \, \text{s} \). How long does the package take to hit the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A particle’s position is given by x = 4t + 2t² and y = 3t² (in meters and seconds). What is the magnitude of its velocity at t = 1 s?

text_solutions:
Velocity components: v_x = dx/dt = 4 + 4t, v_y = dy/dt = 6t.

At t = 1 s: v_x = 4 + 4 × 1 = 8 m/s, v_y = 6 × 1 = 6 m/s.

Speed v = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 m/s.

A force \( \mathbf{F} = 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{N} \) acts at a point with position vector \( \mathbf{r} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 1 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of the torque about the origin?

text_solutions:
Torque: \( \mathbf{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (2 \times 4 - (-1) \times 3) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (8 + 3) = 11 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{Nm} \).

Magnitude = \( 11 \, \text{Nm} \).

qns_content.text: A wire of length \( 6 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 15 \, \Omega \) is stretched to \( 12 \, \text{m} \). What is the new resistance?

New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho l'}{A'} = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = 4 \frac{\rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 15 = 60 \, \Omega \).

qns_content.text: In a closed container, water is in equilibrium with its vapor at 25°C, and the vapor pressure is 0.0313 atm. If the volume of the container is doubled suddenly, what happens to the vapor pressure initially?

text_solutions: Initially, the number of vapor molecules remains the same, but the volume doubles, reducing the pressure to half: \( 0.0313 / 2 = 0.01565 \approx 0.0157 \) atm.

qns_content.text: What is the total number of covalent bonds in \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \), there are 7 single bonds: 5 C-H, 1 C-C, 1 C-N, and 2 N-H. Each single bond is a covalent bond, totaling 7.

text_solutions: Aromatic hydrocarbons contain benzene rings. Benzene (\( \ce{C6H6} \)) is a typical example of an aromatic hydrocarbon.

qns_content.text: The lanthanoid contraction is primarily due to the poor shielding effect of which orbitals?

text_solutions: The 4f orbitals have poor shielding due to their radial distribution, causing a greater effective nuclear charge and size reduction across the lanthanoids.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an allylic halide?

text_solutions: Allylic halides have the halogen atom attached to an sp3-hybridized carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

qns_content.text: Which of the following methods is most suitable for preparing primary alcohols?

text_solutions: Primary alcohols can be synthesized by the reduction of aldehydes using LiAlH4.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?

text_solutions: Sucrose lacks a free aldehyde or ketone group due to the glycosidic bond between C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose, making it non-reducing.

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3NH2} \), the nitrogen forms three single bonds (to C and 2 H) and has one lone pair, indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

qns_content.text: What is the approximate mass of a neutron in unified mass units (u)?

text_solutions: The mass of a neutron is slightly greater than that of a proton. Its approximate value in unified mass units is 1 u, specifically around 1.00867 u, but commonly approximated as 1 u for simplicity.

text_solutions: \( \ce{[Ti(H2O)6]^{3+}} \) (Ti³⁺, \( d^1 \)) absorbs blue-green light due to \( t_{2g} \) to \( e_g \) transition, appearing violet, the complementary color.

qns_content.text: Which of the following undergoes hydrolysis most easily?

text_solutions: Benzylic halides undergo hydrolysis easily due to resonance stabilization.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \)?

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) reacts with propanoyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \)) to form \( \ce{CH3NHCOCH2CH3} \) (N-methylpropanamide) via acylation.

qns_content.text: Which reaction is commonly used for the laboratory preparation of alkanes?

text_solutions: Wurtz reaction involves the reaction of alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether, leading to the formation of higher alkanes.

qns_content.text: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \) and \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Both have the formula \( \ce{C4H9OH} \) but differ in the position of the -OH group (carbon 1 vs. carbon 2), indicating position isomerism.

qns_content.text: For the reaction \(\ce{H2(g) -> 2H(g)}\), what is the entropy change?

text_solutions: Entropy increases as one molecule dissociates into two atoms, increasing disorder.

qns_content.text: What is the bond order of \( \ce{C2} \) according to molecular orbital theory?

text_solutions: For \( \ce{C2} \): 12 electrons, \( (\sigma 1s)^2 (\sigma^* 1s)^2 (\sigma 2s)^2 (\sigma^* 2s)^2 (\pi 2p_x)^2 (\pi 2p_y)^2 \). Bonding = 8, antibonding = 4. Bond order = \( \frac{1}{2} (8 - 4) = 2 \).

qns_content.text: The element with atomic number 21 belongs to which block?

text_solutions: Scandium (Sc, Z=21) has \([Ar] 3d^1 4s^2\), with the last electron in 3d, placing it in the d-block.

qns_content.text: In the reaction \( \ce{4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O} \), how many grams of O₂ are required to react with 17 g of NH₃? (Atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)

text_solutions:
Molar mass of NH₃ = 17 g/mol.

Moles of NH₃ = 17 / 17 = 1 mol.

4 mol NH₃ require 5 mol O₂. Moles of O₂ = (5 / 4) × 1 = 1.25 mol.

Mass = 1.25 × 32 = 40 g.

qns_content.text: Which factor contributes to the extra stability of a half-filled subshell?

text_solutions: Exchange energy, released when electrons with parallel spins exchange positions in degenerate orbitals, enhances stability in half-filled or fully filled subshells.

qns_content.text: For \( \ce{FeO(s) + CO(g) <=> Fe(s) + CO2(g)} \), \( K_p = 0.5 \) atm at 1000 K. If initial \( p_{\ce{CO}} = 1 \) atm, what is \( p_{\ce{CO2}} \) at equilibrium?
Which of the following is a combination redox reaction?

text_solutions: A combination redox reaction involves elements combining, with oxidation and reduction occurring. \( \ce{C + O2 -> CO2} \) has C (0 to +4) oxidized and O (0 to -2) reduced.

qns_content.text: Which of the following properties is NOT characteristic of transition metals?

text_solutions: Transition metals typically have high melting points due to strong metallic bonding involving (n-1)d electrons. Low melting points are not characteristic.

qns_content.text: Which element with atomic number 114 belongs to which block?

text_solutions: Flerovium (Z=114) has the configuration [Rn]5f¹⁴6d¹⁰7s²7p², with the last electron in 7p, placing it in the p-block.

qns_content.text: Which of the following lanthanoids exhibits a +4 oxidation state due to its noble gas configuration?

text_solutions: Cerium (Ce, Z = 58) forms \( \ce{Ce^{4+}} \) with \( 4f^0 \) (noble gas-like), making it stable in this state.

qns_content.text: Which ligand is bidentate?

text_solutions: A bidentate ligand binds through two donor atoms. \( \ce{H2NCH2CH2NH2} \) (ethane-1,2-diamine or en) has two nitrogen atoms that can coordinate, making it bidentate, unlike \( \ce{NH3} \), \( \ce{Cl^-} \), or \( \ce{H2O} \), which are unidentate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following alcohols will show a positive iodoform test?

text_solutions: Alcohols with the structure CH3-C(OH)-R (where R can be H or any alkyl group) give a positive iodoform test.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts benzene to benzophenone?

text_solutions: Friedel-Crafts acylation introduces a ketone functional group into benzene.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) reacts with excess \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \)?

text_solutions: With excess \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) undergoes exhaustive alkylation to form the tertiary amine \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) (triethylamine).

qns_content.text: Which of the following amino acids is not optically active?

text_solutions: Glycine lacks an asymmetric carbon atom (its side chain is -H), making it the only naturally occurring α-amino acid that is not optically active.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds does not undergo nucleophilic addition reaction?

text_solutions: Carboxylic acids do not undergo nucleophilic addition reactions because the carbonyl carbon is less electrophilic due to resonance stabilization.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an industrial application of \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KMnO4} \) is used for bleaching textiles (wool, cotton, silk) due to its strong oxidizing power.

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is most likely to exhibit covalent character in its compounds?

text_solutions: Beryllium (Be), due to its small size and high charge density, forms compounds with significant covalent character (e.g., \(BeCl_2\)).

qns_content.text: How many molecules are in 4 g of H₂? (Molar mass = 2 g/mol, Avogadro number = 6.022 × 10²³)

text_solutions:
Moles = 4 / 2 = 2 mol.

Molecules = 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.2044 × 10²⁴.

qns_content.text: Which of the following types of roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle?

text_solutions: Adventitious roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle, such as in banyan and grass.

qns_content.text: In which type of plants are vascular bundles found scattered throughout the ground tissue?

text_solutions: In monocot stems, vascular bundles are scattered within the ground tissue and lack cambium.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the Golgi apparatus is incorrect?

options.text: The Golgi apparatus packages proteins for secretion.
The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum.

text_solutions: The Golgi apparatus is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins, but it does not synthesize DNA.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a product of the Krebs cycle?

text_solutions: The Krebs cycle produces ATP, NADH, and FADH₂, but glucose is not a product of the cycle.

qns_content.text: Which type of plasticity is exhibited by cotton and coriander due to different leaf forms in juvenile and mature stages?

text_solutions: Cotton and coriander exhibit developmental plasticity, showing different leaf forms during juvenile and mature stages.

qns_content.text: The process of pollen grain germination occurs on the:

text_solutions: Pollen grains land and germinate on the sticky surface of the stigma.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of incomplete dominance?

options.text: Red and white flowers producing pink flowers
Tall and dwarf plants producing all tall offspring
Yellow and green seeds forming only yellow seeds

text_solutions: Incomplete dominance occurs when heterozygous offspring exhibit an intermediate phenotype, as seen in pink flowers from red and white parents.

qns_content.text: What is the structure at the center of a chromosome where spindle fibers attach?

text_solutions: The centromere is the region where spindle fibers attach, aiding in chromosome movement during division.

qns_content.text: Which part of a monocot seed protects the plumule?

text_solutions: The coleoptile is a protective sheath covering the plumule in monocot seeds.

qns_content.text: Which branch of biology deals with classification, nomenclature, and identification of organisms?

text_solutions: Taxonomy is the branch of biology that classifies, names, and identifies organisms systematically.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about plastids?

text_solutions: Amyloplasts are a type of plastid that store starch in plant cells.

qns_content.text: Which molecule is transported from mesophyll cells to bundle sheath cells in C₄ plants?

text_solutions: In C₄ plants, malate is transported from mesophyll cells to bundle sheath cells, where it releases CO₂ for the Calvin cycle.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the male gametophyte in flowering plants?

text_solutions: The pollen grain is the male gametophyte that produces sperm cells in flowering plants.

qns_content.text: What is the purpose of a test cross in genetics?

options.text: To determine the genotype of an individual

text_solutions: A test cross is performed to determine whether an organism is homozygous or heterozygous for a dominant trait.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about genetic disorders is correct?

options.text: Down’s syndrome is caused by trisomy of chromosome 18.
Turner’s syndrome results from an extra Y chromosome.
Klinefelter’s syndrome is caused by the XXY chromosome pattern.

text_solutions: Klinefelter’s syndrome occurs due to an extra X chromosome, leading to a 47, XXY karyotype.

qns_content.text: Which plant growth regulator promotes rapid internode elongation in deepwater rice plants?

text_solutions: Ethylene promotes rapid internode elongation in deepwater rice, enabling the plant to stay above water.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is CORRECT about the Electron Transport Chain (ETC)?

options.text: Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor.
It does not require a proton gradient.

text_solutions: In the Electron Transport Chain, oxygen serves as the final electron acceptor, forming water.

qns_content.text: Which phase of mitosis involves chromosomal condensation?

text_solutions: Prophase is marked by the initiation of chromosomal condensation, making them visible under a microscope.

qns_content.text: Which of the following describes a palmately compound leaf?

options.text: Leaflets are attached at a common point
Leaflets are arranged along a central axis
Leaves are arranged in an alternate phyllotaxy

text_solutions: In palmately compound leaves, leaflets are attached at a common point, as seen in silk cotton.

qns_content.text: Which of the following groups of organisms do not have a true nucleus?

text_solutions: Monerans, including bacteria and archaebacteria, are prokaryotic and lack a well-defined nucleus.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures is unique to monocot leaves?

text_solutions: Bulliform cells in monocot leaves help in minimizing water loss by curling the leaves under drought conditions.

qns_content.text: Which microtubule arrangement is characteristic of eukaryotic cilia and flagella?

text_solutions: The axoneme of eukaryotic cilia and flagella shows a 9+2 arrangement of microtubules, consisting of nine peripheral doublets and two central microtubules.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme is absent in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants?

text_solutions: In C₄ plants, RuBisCO is absent in mesophyll cells and is present only in bundle sheath cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about codons is incorrect?

options.text: Codons in mRNA bind to tRNA anticodons during translation.
Each codon codes for more than one amino acid.

text_solutions: Each codon codes for only one specific amino acid, not multiple amino acids.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a correct statement about ecosystem stability?

options.text: Ecosystem stability is not influenced by species interactions.
Ecosystem stability depends only on abiotic factors.
Ecosystem stability is unaffected by human activities.

text_solutions: Higher biodiversity enhances ecosystem resilience by increasing species interactions and functional redundancy.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents net primary productivity (NPP)?

text_solutions: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the biomass available to consumers and is calculated as Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus Respiration (R).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding co-dominance?

options.text: Both alleles are equally expressed in the heterozygous condition.
AB blood group is an example of co-dominance.
One allele completely masks the other in co-dominance.

text_solutions: In co-dominance, both alleles are equally expressed rather than one masking the other.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures disappears during prophase of mitosis?

text_solutions: During prophase, the nuclear envelope breaks down, allowing chromosomes to move freely within the cell.

qns_content.text: In which type of inflorescence are older flowers at the base and younger ones at the tip?

text_solutions: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow, and older flowers are found at the base while younger ones are at the tip.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about viruses is correct?

options.text: Viruses are considered living only inside a host cell

text_solutions: Viruses are considered living only when inside a host cell, where they use the host’s machinery to replicate.

qns_content.text: Which component of the plasma membrane contributes to its fluidity?

text_solutions: The phospholipid bilayer contributes to membrane fluidity by allowing lateral movement of molecules.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the leading and lagging strands is correct?

options.text: Both strands are synthesized in the 3' to 5' direction.
The lagging strand is synthesized in Okazaki fragments.

text_solutions: The lagging strand is synthesized in short fragments called Okazaki fragments, while the leading strand is synthesized continuously.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes commensalism?

options.text: One species benefits, the other is unaffected
One species benefits, the other is harmed

text_solutions: In commensalism, one species benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of an alien invasive species affecting biodiversity?

text_solutions: Lantana camara is an invasive species that disrupts native biodiversity by outcompeting indigenous plants.

qns_content.text: Which type of diversity includes genetic variation within a single species?

text_solutions: Genetic diversity refers to variations in the genetic makeup within a species, allowing adaptation to different environmental conditions.

qns_content.text: What is the full form of VNTR, a key concept in DNA fingerprinting?

text_solutions: VNTR stands for Variable Number of Tandem Repeats, which are used in DNA fingerprinting due to their high polymorphism.

qns_content.text: During which stage of mitosis do chromatids get separated?

text_solutions: During anaphase, the centromeres split, and sister chromatids separate, moving to opposite poles of the cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following tissues provides mechanical support and flexibility?

text_solutions: Collenchyma provides mechanical support while allowing flexibility in young stems and leaves.

qns_content.text: Which type of placentation is observed in sunflower?

text_solutions: Sunflower exhibits basal placentation, where a single ovule is attached to the base of the ovary.

qns_content.text: Which group of pteridophytes is known for producing microphyllous leaves?

text_solutions: Lycopsida (e.g., Selaginella) is characterized by the presence of small, simple, and scale-like microphyllous leaves.

qns_content.text: Which external factor is rarely a limiting factor for photosynthesis under natural conditions?

text_solutions: Light is rarely a limiting factor in nature because plants require only about 10% of full sunlight for photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a stop codon?

text_solutions: UAA is a stop codon that signals the termination of translation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of species diversity?

options.text: Variety of bird species in the Amazon

text_solutions: Species diversity refers to the variety of different species within an ecosystem, such as the diverse bird species in the Amazon rainforest.

qns_content.text: What is the expected phenotypic ratio of a dihybrid cross in F2 generation?

text_solutions: A dihybrid cross results in a phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1 in the F2 generation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the "Sixth Extinction" is correct?

options.text: It is caused mainly by human activities

text_solutions: The current "Sixth Extinction" is primarily driven by human activities, such as habitat destruction and over-exploitation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about the function of the SA node?

options.text: It generates impulses that regulate heart contractions.
It delays the impulses before they reach the ventricles.
It is located in the left ventricle.
It prevents blood backflow in the heart.

text_solutions: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the natural pacemaker of the heart and initiates electrical impulses for contraction.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by Plasmodium species?

text_solutions: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium species and is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about genetically modified organisms (GMOs) is incorrect?

options.text: GMOs are created using recombinant DNA technology.
GMOs can be used to produce pharmaceuticals.
GMOs can be used in agriculture to improve crop yield.

text_solutions: GMOs have significant applications in medicine, including the production of insulin, vaccines, and other therapeutic proteins.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a structural polysaccharide in fungi?

text_solutions: Chitin is a structural polysaccharide found in fungal cell walls and the exoskeleton of arthropods.

qns_content.text: Which skeletal component protects the brain?

text_solutions: The cranium is a bony structure that encloses and protects the brain.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC)?

options.text: GEAC regulates the use of genetically modified organisms in India.
GEAC is an international body for genetic research.

text_solutions: The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC) is responsible for regulating the use, approval, and safety of genetically modified organisms in India.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus?

text_solutions: Infectious mononucleosis, also known as the "kissing disease," is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the thalamus is correct?

options.text: It acts as a relay station for sensory information.
It is responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid.
It has no role in sensory processing.

text_solutions: The thalamus serves as a relay station for sensory signals, directing them to the appropriate areas in the cerebral cortex.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA) is correct?

options.text: JGA regulates blood pressure by releasing renin.
JGA is located in the Loop of Henle.
JGA decreases renin secretion when blood pressure is low.

text_solutions: The juxtaglomerular apparatus regulates blood pressure by secreting renin, which activates the renin-angiotensin system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following animals is a member of phylum Mollusca?

text_solutions: Octopus belongs to phylum Mollusca and is a member of class Cephalopoda.

qns_content.text: What is the function of the nictitating membrane in frogs?

text_solutions: The nictitating membrane protects the frog’s eyes underwater and keeps them moist.

qns_content.text: Which of the following proteins helps in osmotic balance of blood?

text_solutions: Albumin helps maintain osmotic balance by regulating water movement in and out of blood vessels.

qns_content.text: Which part of a sarcomere disappears during complete muscle contraction?

text_solutions: The H-zone disappears during full contraction as actin filaments slide over myosin.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the cilia lining the fallopian tubes?

options.text: Transport of the ovum toward the uterus

text_solutions: The cilia in the fallopian tubes help move the ovum from the ovary toward the uterus.

qns_content.text: Which concept in evolution explains the formation of species from a common ancestor in different geographical regions?

text_solutions: Adaptive radiation explains the formation of species from a common ancestor as they adapt to different geographical regions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about polymerase chain reaction (PCR)?

options.text: PCR is used to amplify specific DNA sequences.
PCR is used to degrade foreign DNA in cells.

text_solutions: PCR is a technique used to amplify specific DNA sequences through cycles of denaturation, annealing, and extension.

qns_content.text: Which factor is the primary cause of population explosion in India?

text_solutions: The population explosion in India is primarily due to a decreased infant mortality rate and an increased life expectancy.

qns_content.text: What is the main function of the pleural fluid in the lungs?

text_solutions: Pleural fluid reduces friction between the lung surface and the thoracic cavity during breathing.

qns_content.text: Which vitamin is an essential part of the coenzyme NAD?

text_solutions: Vitamin B3 (Niacin) is a key component of NAD (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide).

qns_content.text: Which of the following animals belongs to the phylum Hemichordata?

text_solutions: Balanoglossus is a hemichordate, characterized by a proboscis, collar, and trunk.

qns_content.text: Which macromolecule serves as the genetic material in all living organisms?

text_solutions: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) serves as the genetic material in all living organisms.

qns_content.text: Which mechanism prevents polyspermy after the first sperm fuses with the oocyte?

text_solutions: The cortical reaction, which occurs immediately after the first sperm fuses with the oocyte, causes changes in the zona pellucida that prevent further sperm penetration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect?

options.text: Adaptive radiation results in species diversity from a common ancestor.
Genetic drift has a significant impact on small populations.
Homologous organs arise due to convergent evolution.

text_solutions: Homologous organs arise due to divergent evolution, not convergent evolution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about passive immunity is incorrect?

options.text: Passive immunity is acquired through antibody transfer.
Passive immunity can be provided by maternal antibodies.

text_solutions: Passive immunity does not involve memory cell formation; it provides temporary protection using ready-made antibodies.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about gel electrophoresis is incorrect?

options.text: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments based on their size.
Smaller DNA fragments migrate faster than larger fragments.
Gel electrophoresis does not require a gel matrix.

text_solutions: Gel electrophoresis requires a gel matrix (commonly agarose) to separate DNA fragments based on size.

qns_content.text: Which term refers to the generation of identical plants through tissue culture?

text_solutions: Micropropagation is the process of producing large numbers of genetically identical plants through tissue culture.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is responsible for stimulating the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine?

text_solutions: TSH, secreted by the anterior pituitary, stimulates the thyroid gland to release thyroxine (T4).

qns_content.text: Which part of the nervous system is responsible for transmitting impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles?

text_solutions: The somatic nervous system controls voluntary movements by transmitting impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles.

qns_content.text: Which organ in humans plays a primary role in excretion?

text_solutions: Kidneys are the primary excretory organs that remove nitrogenous wastes and help in osmoregulation.

qns_content.text: Which class of enzymes catalyzes the joining of two molecules?

text_solutions: Ligases catalyze the joining of two molecules, often requiring ATP.

qns_content.text: Which polysaccharide serves as an energy storage molecule in animals?

text_solutions: Glycogen is the primary storage polysaccharide in animals and fungi.

qns_content.text: Which fetal membrane encloses the developing embryo and is filled with amniotic fluid?

text_solutions: The amnion is the membrane that forms the amniotic sac, which contains the amniotic fluid protecting the embryo.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about inflammation is incorrect?

options.text: Inflammation increases blood supply to affected tissues.
Inflammation is a key part of the immune response.

text_solutions: Inflammation is a necessary immune response that helps in pathogen elimination and tissue repair.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about gene cloning is incorrect?

options.text: Gene cloning involves the insertion of foreign DNA into a vector.
Gene cloning can be used to produce recombinant proteins.
Gene cloning cannot be used for medical research.
Gene cloning requires the use of restriction enzymes and ligases.

text_solutions: Gene cloning has numerous applications in medical research, including gene therapy and pharmaceutical production.

qns_content.text: Which hybrid plant is formed by the fusion of protoplasts of tomato and potato?

text_solutions: Pomato is formed by the fusion of protoplasts from tomato and potato plants through somatic hybridization.

qns_content.text: Which term is used to describe the autonomous replication of a plasmid inside a bacterial cell?

text_solutions: Autonomous replication allows plasmids to multiply independently of the bacterial chromosome.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect?

options.text: Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies.
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium remains stable even with continuous mutations.
Mutation is a source of genetic variation.
Darwin’s theory emphasizes survival of the fittest.

text_solutions: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is disrupted by mutations, gene flow, genetic drift, and natural selection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following bones is a part of the pelvic girdle?

text_solutions: The ilium is a part of the pelvic girdle, while the humerus, scapula, and clavicle are part of the appendicular skeleton​.

qns_content.text: During which process do frogs burrow in the summer to avoid extreme heat?

text_solutions: Frogs undergo aestivation, also known as summer sleep, to escape extreme heat.

qns_content.text: Which of the following animals belongs to the phylum Arthropoda?

text_solutions: Limulus (King crab) belongs to phylum Arthropoda and is considered a living fossil.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about frog locomotion is incorrect?

options.text: Frogs have strong hind limbs adapted for jumping and swimming.
Frogs have webbed feet that help in swimming.
Forelimbs are longer than hind limbs for efficient jumping.
Frogs use their forelimbs for landing and balance after jumping.

text_solutions: The hind limbs in frogs are longer and more muscular than the forelimbs to aid in jumping.

qns_content.text: Which among the following is the most abundant protein in the biosphere?

text_solutions: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the biosphere.

qns_content.text: Which endocrine gland is responsible for the secretion of insulin and glucagon?

text_solutions: The pancreas contains the Islets of Langerhans, which secrete insulin and glucagon to regulate blood glucose levels.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about hormonal contraceptive pills is incorrect?

options.text: Hormonal contraceptive pills alter cervical mucus consistency.
Hormonal contraceptive pills may prevent implantation of a fertilized egg.

text_solutions: Hormonal contraceptive pills do not permanently stop menstruation; their effects are reversible.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is primarily responsible for secreting progesterone during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle?

text_solutions: The corpus luteum forms after ovulation and secretes progesterone, which prepares the endometrium for implantation.
